best_season: Late June through September is the primary climbing season. Late June through early July is particularly recommended to avoid late-summer snow and to ensure adequate daylight for the long descent. Avoid early season (June) when snow patches and ice may still be present at the base.

June through October offers the most reliable conditions per route reports, with the window potentially stretching from May into November depending on that year's snowpack. Early-season parties should expect lingering snow on the approach and the off-trail scramble slopes.
Late spring through fall (roughly July-October); the ridge and approach basin are typically snow-free from around mid-July, with stable weather often continuing into September or October.

approach: Same trailhead and trail as True Grit: Sunrise Mine Trail #707 from the Sunrise Mine Trailhead on the Mountain Loop Highway, through second-growth forest and an early creek crossing of the South Fork Stillaguamish (log crossing, harder in high runoff), up through Wirtz Basin and out onto open, cairned talus, then through Headlee Pass (~4,720 ft, 2.7 mi, loose rock/rockfall exposure in the narrow couloir) and down to Vesper Creek and Vesper Lake (Lake Elan, ~4,950 ft, ~3.5 mi/~2,700 ft gain) — the last dependable water. From the lake the maintained trail fades; cross the outlet and follow an obvious talus ridgeline up to the col/saddle between Vesper and Wolf Peak. From there a slightly improbable but well-trodden heather ledge system (goat trail through it) cuts across the north face at roughly 5,800 ft to a small notch overlooking the remnant Vesper Glacier, where the route starts. This traverse crosses steep, exposed heather that's treacherous when wet and typically holds snow into mid-to-late summer, so an ice axe (and sometimes crampons) is worth carrying into early summer. Plan on 3+ hours from the trailhead to the base of the climb.
